title: The Diphthongs
subtitle: Six combinations that act as single vowels.
objectives: Recognize and pronounce the six Latin diphthongs: ae, oe, au, ei, eu, ui.
Distinguish diphthongs from separate vowels by pronunciation and spelling.
Identify diphthongs inside real Latin words.
Read aloud words containing diphthongs with correct stress.

sections.heading: What is a diphthong
sections.body:
A diphthong is two vowels pronounced as a single syllable. In English, the word 'coin' has a diphthong (oi); the word 'co-operate' has two separate vowels (o-o). Latin has six diphthongs. They appear frequently, especially ae and au.

The six diphthongs:
  ae — like the i in 'aisle'
  oe — like the oi in 'oil'
  au — like the ou in 'out'
  ei — like the ay in 'say' (rare)
  eu — like eh-oo said quickly (rare)
  ui — like we in 'we' (very rare)

Of these, ae and au dominate. You will see them dozens of times on every page of Latin. The others appear in a handful of words: ei in hei and deinde, eu in heu and neuter, ui in cui and huic.

sections.heading: The spelling of ae and oe
sections.body:
In medieval manuscripts and in modern printed editions before the nineteenth century, ae and oe were often written as ligatures: æ and œ. In this course we write them as two letters: ae, oe. The pronunciation is the same.

Two common words illustrate the difference between a diphthong and two separate vowels:
  poena (punishment) — diphthong, one syllable: POE-na
  poēta (poet) — two separate vowels, three syllables: po-AY-ta

The macron over the e in poēta signals that the o and e belong to separate syllables. Without it, you would read 'poena' and expect a punishment, not a poem.

sections.heading: Listening drill
sections.instructions: Each diphthong is spoken in isolation, then inside a real Latin word. Repeat after the recording.

sections.heading: Self-check
sections.instructions: Without looking back, answer each question.

items.prompt: How many diphthongs does Latin have?
items.answer: Six: ae, oe, au, ei, eu, ui.

items.prompt: Which two diphthongs are most common?
What is the difference between poena and poēta?
items.answer: poena has a diphthong (oe) and two syllables; poēta has two separate vowels and three syllables.

items.prompt: Why is a macron sometimes written over one vowel in what looks like a diphthong?
items.answer: To signal that the vowels belong to separate syllables and do not form a diphthong.

sections.heading: Words with diphthongs
sections.instructions: Read each word aloud. Each contains at least one diphthong.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can pronounce all six diphthongs without hesitation and identify them inside words.
